title: Probabilistic geo-favoring router with capacity signals and SLO-aware shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Traffic spikes and regional maintenance have exposed brittle binary geo-pinning behavior. Requests either stay pinned to a preferred region and face queue/backpressure, or immediately fail over causing cold-start latency and cache misses. We need a routing policy that prefers local/affinity regions but gracefully degrades using probabilistic diversion based on live capacity signals and observed tail latency, with explicit circuit-breaker and load-shed hooks to protect SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce high-p90/p99 latency during regional pressure while preserving affinity for locality and KV cache hit rates.
- Ensure predictable graceful degradation with clear SLO impact boundaries.
- Provide knobs for canary, rollout, and emergency shed.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of existing steering service. Iteration on top of current steering decision path.
- Solving cold-start in model pools (separate infra work).

Design summary:
1) Scoring function: compute per-region score = w_latency * normalized_latency + w_capacity * capacity_headroom_score + w_affinity * affinity_bonus + w_penalty * recent_error_rate_penalty. Scores normalized to [0,1].
2) Probabilistic selection: convert scores to selection probabilities using softmax with temperature T. Temperature is a rollout knob (high T => more exploration).
3) Capacity signals: use autoscaler and pool occupancy metrics (GPU_util, queue_depth, inflight) to compute headroom. Headroom below hard threshold triggers region circuit-breaker.
4) Circuit breakers: three-state per-region breaker (Closed -> Open -> Half-Open). Open when persistent capacity pressure or error-rate breach for N windows. Half-open allows limited probe volume.
5) SLO-aware shedding: when global/route-level SLO risk detected (projected p99 > threshold or queue crossing), begin probabilistic shed of low-priority requests using policy buckets (best-effort classes). Shedding is prioritized by request class metadata (real-time, batch, background).
6) KV cache-awareness: affinity_bonus decays with time since last cache hit; routing tracks per-user prefix hit-rate signal aggregated by region to encourage cache locality.
7) Fallback model variants: when exact model variant unavailable, prefer compatible lower-capacity variant as a fallback; steering incorporates variant compatibility score in region scoring.

Telemetry and alerts:
- New dashboards: per-region score distribution, temperature, circuit-breaker states, shed-rate, per-route SLO projection.
- Alerts: region circuit-breaker Open for > 2m, shed rate > 10% for production routes, projected p99 exceedance for > 5m.
- Synthetic canary: cross-region synthetic traffic exercising pin/unpin and cold cache cases.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged implementation behind steering.v2 flag.
- Stage 0: simulation mode (traffic replayer) to validate decisions offline against last 72h telemetry.
- Stage 1: Canary to 5% of traffic (low-risk routes) for 48h, monitor cache-hit delta, p50/p95/p99.
- Stage 2: Gradual ramp to 25% then 60% across regions with canary expansion and ops validation.
- Fail-open criteria: immediate rollback if shed rate spikes or p99 worsens > 25% relative baseline.

Acceptance notes: Implementation must include config knobs accessible via Console and an audit log of steering flips for Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated replay shows p99 improvements or no regression on 72h traffic traces
Canary demonstrates stable or improved p50/p95 and shed rate under load
Console exposes temperature and per-region circuit-breaker states
Automated tests for circuit-breaker transitions and probabilistic selection logic
Runbook updated with rollback and mitigation steps
